SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p428/r1.anchor: صيّره على أحسن ما يكون في الصورة والمعنى والإدراك

ELMALILI:95:4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r1.claim: God created the human species in the best form of bodily and spiritual shaping, ordering, and development; the phrase is a stable adverbial state of the human being.
ELMALILI:95:4/r1.anchor: insan cinsini maddeten ve mânen doğrultmanın, kıvâma koymanın, biçimlendirmenin en güzelinde

ELMALILI:95:4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r2.claim: Taqwīm means straightening, ordering, strengthening, or valuing; the indefinite wording intensifies the phrase to encompass every kind of excellence.
ELMALILI:95:4/r2.anchor: eğriyi doğrultmak, kıvâma, nizâma koymak, kuvvet biçmek, kıymetlendirmek mânalarına gelir

ELMALILI:95:4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r3.speaker: النخعي، مجاهد، قتادة
ELMALILI:95:4/r3.claim: Al-Baḥr reports that al-Nakhaʿī, Mujāhid, and Qatāda understand the verse as beauty of human form and senses.
ELMALILI:95:4/r3.anchor: Nehaî ve Mücâhid ve Katâde suret ve havâssının güzelliği demişler

ELMALILI:95:4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r4.claim: Another reported gloss is the straightness of the human stature.

ELMALILI:95:4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r5.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
ELMALILI:95:4/r5.claim: Abū Bakr b. Ṭāhir interprets the best form as adornment with intellect, understanding, and discernment.
ELMALILI:95:4/r5.anchor: Ebû Bekir b. Tâhir akl ü idrak ve temyiz ile tezyîni demiş

ELMALILI:95:4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r6.speaker: عكرمة
ELMALILI:95:4/r6.claim: ʿIkrima understands the best form as youth and strength.
ELMALILI:95:4/r6.anchor: İkrime de şebâbı ve kuvveti demiş

ELMALILI:95:4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r7.speaker: البحر
ELMALILI:95:4/r7.claim: Al-Baḥr's preferred meaning includes every excellence, both bodily beauty and the capacities of intellect and character.

ELMALILI:95:4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r8.claim: Humanity is a comprehensive sign that joins the unseen and visible realms and contains the meanings of the world's wonders and divine secrets.
ELMALILI:95:4/r8.anchor: gayb u şehadet mecrâlarının mecma‘ı, ifade ve istifade felekleri neyyireyninin matla‘ı

ELMALILI:95:4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r9.speaker: علي
ELMALILI:95:4/r9.claim: A saying attributed to ʿAlī says that a person's remedy and disease are within, and that the greater world is folded inside the supposedly small human body.

ELMALILI:95:4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r10.claim: Human beauty is not merely outward form: it lies in feeling and recognizing beauty, knowing God as the absolutely beautiful, and acquiring divine character; this is humanity's intended perfection.
ELMALILI:95:4/r10.anchor: insanın güzelliği ahsen-i takvîmde olması duygusuz olan şekl ü suretinde değil, duygusunda

ELMALILI:95:4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r11.claim: Humans are created with the capacity to rise toward this perfection, not born already complete; otherwise no mortality or lowliness would be observable.
ELMALILI:95:4/r11.anchor: İnsan ilk doğuşunda bu kemâlde olarak değil, fakat bu kıvâma, bu kemâle

ELMALILI:95:4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:4/r12.claim: People begin with burdens and imperfections to shed: some purify themselves and rise, while many lose their share of beauty and sink toward the lowest ranks.
ELMALILI:95:4/r12.anchor: birtakımlarının yükselmesine mukabil diğer birçoklarının da hiçbir hisse-i hüsnü kalmayarak en sefil derekelere kadar yuvarlanıp durduğu

ELMALILI:95:4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:4/r13.speaker: قاضي يحيى بن أكثم، الحنفية
ELMALILI:95:4/r13.claim: A report says Qāḍī Yaḥyā b. Aktham and some Ḥanafīs ruled no divorce occurred when a man conditioned divorce on his wife not being more beautiful than the moon, arguing from this verse.
ELMALILI:95:4/r13.anchor: Kādî Yahya b. Eksem ve bazı Hanefiyye

ELMALILI:95:6-8/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r13.claim: The surah establishes human creation and religion, summarizes the preceding surahs, and prepares for the next; beginning the next surah with Read in your Lord's name is fitting because religion is true and God is the best judge.
ELMALILI:95:6-8/r13.anchor: hem evvelki sûreler bir hulâsaya bağlanmış, hem de bundan sonraki sûrelere bir temhid yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r1.claim: God swears by four signs of His knowledge, artistry, and power—fig and olive as bodily food, Sinai as revelation's spiritual food, and secure Mecca—to affirm that He made humans best and endowed them to bear physical and spiritual duties (cf. 17:70).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r1.anchor: incire, zeytine, mânevî gıdası olan vahyin indiği Sînâ dağına ve “emin belde”ye (Mekke), insanların muhtaç oldukları maddî ve mânevî ikramların mükemmel örneklerine yemin ederek insanı en güzel biçimde yarattığını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r7.claim: Ahsan taqwim means the finest, most complete human form and structure, making people the most excellent earthly creatures physically, spiritually, and intellectually.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r7.anchor: insana Allah tarafından verilen en güzel ve en mükemmel biçim ve yapıyı, bu sayede insanın, yeryüzü varlıkları içinde gerek fizyolojik gerekse ruhsal ve zihinsel yetenekler bakımdan en mükemmel ve en seçkin canlı olarak yaratılmış olmasını ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r8.claim: Human excellence reflects God's favors: creating the human with His hand, breathing His spirit (38:72, 38:75), creating in His image, and making humans vicegerents (2:30).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r8.anchor: Allah’ın onu kendi eliyle yaratıp ruhundan üflemesi (bk. Sâd 38/72, 75), “kendi sûreti üzere”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r9.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r9.claim: Commentators see humans as God's most beautiful creatures: living, knowing, willing, speaking, hearing, seeing, reasoning, and governing, they master stronger beings and build cultures; these traits reflect some divine attributes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:95:1/r9.anchor: Müfessirler Allah’ın insandan daha güzel mahlûku olmadığı kanaatindedirler. Zira Allah insanı canlı, bilen, irade sahibi, konuşan, işiten, dinleyen, gören, düşünüp tedbir alan

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p407/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p407/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p407/r3.claim: Humans are created in the best mould and can become God's best creatures by recognizing their worth, but indifference can reduce them to the lowest; their ascent and descent have no limit, hence the sages' counsel to know oneself.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p407/r3.anchor: The Almighty has created him in the best of moulds with great abilities.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r1.claim: Surat al-Tin is also called al-Tin without the conjunction; most say it is Meccan, while Qatada and a report from Ibn Abbas call it Medinan. The reference to the secure city is unanimously taken as Mecca, supporting the majority; all agree on eight verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r1.anchor: ويقال لها سورة التين بلا واو مكية في قول الجمهور وعن قتادة أنها مدنية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r2.claim: After the preceding surah described Muhammad as the most perfect human, this surah discusses humanity's condition and end and God's reward for those who follow that exemplary figure.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p173/r2.anchor: لما ذكر سبحانه في السورة السابقة حال أكمل النوع الإنساني بالإتفاق بل أكمل خلق الله

TAB:95:4/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r1.speaker: author
TAB:95:4/r1.claim: The statement about creating humanity in the best form is the answer to the oath by the fig and olive.
TAB:95:4/r1.anchor: وهذا جواب القسم ،   يقول تعالى ذكره :  والتين والزيتون

TAB:95:4/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:95:4/r2.claim: Qatada also identifies this clause as the answer to the oath.
TAB:95:4/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قال :  وقع القسم هاهنا

TAB:95:4/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:95:4/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the phrase as the most balanced creation.
TAB:95:4/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس فِي أحسن تقويم قال :  في أعدل خلق

TAB:95:4/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB:95:4/r4.claim: Ibrahim glosses it as the best form.
TAB:95:4/r4.anchor: عن حماد ،   عن إبراهيم ( لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم ) قال :  في أحسن صورة

TAB:95:4/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r5.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB:95:4/r5.claim: A further report from Ibrahim glosses the phrase simply as creation.
TAB:95:4/r5.anchor: عن حماد ،   عن إبراهيم في ( أحسن تقويم ) قال :  خلق

TAB:95:4/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB:95:4/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliya says it means the best form.
TAB:95:4/r6.anchor: عن أبي العالية ف( ِي أحسن تقويم ) يقول :  في أحسن صورة

TAB:95:4/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:95:4/r7.claim: Mujahid says it means the best form.
TAB:95:4/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد ( فِي أحسن تقويم ) :  في أحسن صورة

TAB:95:4/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:95:4/r8.claim: In another report, Mujahid calls it the best creation.
TAB:95:4/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قوله :  ( فِي أحسن تقويم ) قال :  في أحسن خلق

TAB:95:4/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r9.speaker: قتادة
TAB:95:4/r9.claim: Qatada interprets the phrase as the best form.
TAB:95:4/r9.anchor: عن قتادة ( فِي أحسن تقويم ) يقول :  في أحسن صورة

TAB:95:4/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r10.speaker: الكلبي
TAB:95:4/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi shares the view that it means the best form.
TAB:95:4/r10.anchor: عن معمر ،   عن قتادة ،   هو والكلبي ( فِي أحسن تقويم ) قالا :  في أحسن صورة

TAB:95:4/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r11.speaker: عكرمة
TAB:95:4/r11.claim: Ikrima interprets it as the young person's strongest and most vigorous stage.
TAB:95:4/r11.anchor: عن عكرمة ،   في قوله :  ( لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم ) قال :  الشاب القوي الجلد

TAB:95:4/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:95:4/r12.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas points to the beginning of a person's youth.
TAB:95:4/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس ( لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم ) قال :  شبابه أول ما نشأ

TAB:95:4/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:95:4/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas also says humans are distinguished because other creatures are face-down while the human stands upright.
TAB:95:4/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس( لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم ) قال :  خلق كل شيء منكبا على وجهه

TAB:95:4/r14.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:95:4/r14.speaker: author
TAB:95:4/r14.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that humanity was created in the best and most balanced form; he reads ‘best form’ as an adjective for an omitted ‘form,’ effectively ‘in the best formation.’
TAB:95:4/r14.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب :  أن يقال :  إن معنى ذلك

BURHAN:v4p251/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p251/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p251/r2.claim: The basic sense of باء is attachment: literally one thing joins another, and figuratively a person passes by a place adjacent to them.
BURHAN:v4p251/r2.anchor: أصله للإلصاق ومعناه اختلاط الشيء بالشيء ويكون حقيقة وهو الأكثر

ITQAN:v2p538/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p538/r1.speaker: سوار بن شبيب
ITQAN:v2p538/r1.claim: Sawwar ibn Shabib reports from Ibn al-Zubayr that Umar considered unifying recitation after people differed; later Uthman assembled codices, had the sheets checked with Aisha, and ordered the other copies destroyed.
ITQAN:v2p538/r1.anchor: عن سوار بن شبيب قال سألت ابن الزبير عن المصاحف فقال قام رجل إلى عمر فقال يا أمير المؤمنين إن الناس قد اختلفوا

ITQAN:v2p538/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p538/r2.speaker: عبد الأعلى بن عبد الله بن عامر
ITQAN:v2p538/r2.claim: Abd al-Ala ibn Abdullah ibn Amir reports that after the codex was completed, Uthman praised the work but said there was something they would correct with their tongues.
ITQAN:v2p538/r2.anchor: عن عبد الأعلى ابن عبد الله بن عامر قال لما فرغ من المصحف أتي به عثمان

ITQAN:v2p538/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p538/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p538/r3.claim: Suyuti says the reports are compatible: Uthman saw the codex just after it was written, noticed a form outside Quraysh usage such as التابوة for التابوت, then corrected it in the later review; later transmitters may have garbled his words.
ITQAN:v2p538/r3.anchor: فكأنه عرض عليه عقب الفراغ من كتابته فرأى فيه شيئا كتب على غير لسان قريش كما وقع لهم في التابوة والتابوت

ITQAN:v2p538/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p538/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p538/r4.claim: The first report shows that the codices were accurately checked and left no need for repair; Aisha’s report has a sound chain, so weakening it does not answer the issue.
ITQAN:v2p538/r4.anchor: فهذا يدل على أنهم ضبطوها وأتقنوها ولم يتركوا فيها ما يحتاج إلى إصلاح ولا تقويم

ITQAN:v2p538/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p538/r5.speaker: ابن أشته وابن جبارة
ITQAN:v2p538/r5.claim: Ibn Ashtah and Ibn Jabara explain Aisha’s “they erred” as choosing less than the best of the seven ahruf for unification, not writing an impermissible mistake; consensus would have rejected an invalid text.
ITQAN:v2p538/r5.anchor: وتبعه ابن جبارة في شرح الرائية بأن معنى قولها أخطئوا أي في اختيار الأولى من الأحرف السبعة لجمع الناس عليه

ITQAN:v2p538/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p538/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v2p538/r6.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains “a grammatical error by the scribe” as the scribe’s dialect and reading, alongside another reading.
ITQAN:v2p538/r6.anchor: وأما قول سعيد بن جبير لحن من الكاتب فيعني باللحن القراءة واللغة يعني أنها لغة الذي كتبها وقراءته

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p90/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p90/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p90/r1.claim: Routine correctness is no rhetorical merit by itself; a real distinction requires artful choice and a subtle, difficult-to-reach correctness, and comparison must separate verbal craft from composition.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p90/r1.anchor: حتى يشرف موضعه ، ويصعب الوصول إليه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p90/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p90/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p90/r2.claim: In Ibn al-Muʿtazz’s verse, the grace comes not simply from saying the gaze “leaps,” but from the arrangement: the opening, emphatic lām, مني, نظرة rather than النظر, ثم, and the intervening phrase between inna and its predicate.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p90/r2.anchor: ليس هو لذلك ، بل لأن قال في أول البيت : ' وإني '

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r1.claim: If most Qurʾānic wording were rare, it could not establish inimitability: people familiar with rare words could answer with comparable obscurities, such as الشوقب مقابل الشوذب or الأمق مقابل الأشق.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r1.anchor: فلو تحدي به من يعلم أمثاله لم يتعذر عليه أن يعارضه بمثله

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r2.claim: Challenging people ignorant of the rare vocabulary would be like challenging Arabs to speak Turkish, so obscurity cannot be the basis of the Qurʾān’s challenge.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r2.anchor: ولو تحدي به من لا علم له بأمثال ما فيه من الغريب كان ذلك بمنزلة أن يتحدى العرب إلى أن يتكلموا بلسان الترك

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r3.speaker: عمر رضي الله عنه
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r3.claim: ʿUmar praised Zuhayr for avoiding verbal complexity and not pursuing obscure vocabulary, treating both as faults to avoid.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r3.anchor: قول عمر رضي الله عنه في زهير : إنه كان لا يعاظل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r4.speaker: الجاحظ
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r4.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ reports that al-Ḥajjāj doubted that Yazīd authored a letter full of rare diction, summoned Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, and questioned how he had acquired such eloquence after learning he was born in al-Ahwāz.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r4.anchor: وقال الجاحظ في كتاب البيان والتبيين : ورأيت الناس يتداولون رسالة يحيى بن يعمر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r5.claim: The author rejects the story of Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar’s obscure rebuke to a litigating woman as an example of eloquence: if it was transmitted to prove eloquence, it is far from that quality.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r5.anchor: وإن كانوا قد رووا هذا الكلام لكي يدل على فصاحة وبلاغة فقد باعده الله من صفة البلاغة والفصاحة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r6.claim: Critics mistakenly treat qualities acquired through meaning as qualities inherent in words themselves, confusing linguistic form with effects produced by what a phrase means.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r6.anchor: وهو ظنهم الذي ظنوه في اللفظ ، وجعلهم الأوصاف التي تجري عليه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r7.claim: The relevant eloquence is not correct pronunciation or freedom from grammatical error, but subtle merits understood through thought; comparison assumes both expressions are already free of error.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r7.anchor: ولكن من أجل لطائف تدرك بالفهم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r8.claim: There is no comparative merit in inflection when both expressions are correct: the difference is only that one may contain an error while the other remains correct, not that one excels in iʿrāb.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p296/r8.anchor: وجدنا التفاضل فيه محالا لأنه لا يتصور أن يكون للرفع والنصب في كلام مزية

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r1.claim: The author rejects the common view that ordinary habit makes meaning the sole criterion; identifying a composition’s merits is a separate critical skill.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r1.anchor: لم نرى متقدما في علم البلاغة مبرزا في شأوها إلا وهو ينكر هذا الرأي

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r2.speaker: البحتري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r2.claim: When asked whether Muslim or Abū Nuwās was the better poet, al-Buḥturī chose Abū Nuwās and said Thaʿlab and other poetry scholars lacked the practiced experience needed to judge poetry’s difficulties and demands.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r2.anchor: ما روي عن البحتري : روي أن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن طاهر سأله عن مسلم وأبي نواس أيهما أشعر ؟ فقال : أبو نواس

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r3.speaker: البحتري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r3.claim: A second report begins with al-Buḥturī questioning someone who brought al-Shanfara’s poems to Thaʿlab; he then distinguishes Thaʿlab’s expertise in parsing and rare words from critical taste, asking where poetry with “veins of gold” is.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r3.anchor: رآني البحتري ومعي دفتر شعر فقال : ما هذا ؟ فقلت : شعر الشنفرى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r4.speaker: الشاعر
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r4.claim: A quoted poet likens those who merely carry poems without knowing their excellence to camels, illustrating the difference between transmitting poetry and discerning its quality.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p195/r4.anchor: زوامل للأشعار لا علم عندهم بجيدها إلا كعلم الأباعر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p317/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p317/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p317/r1.claim: Metaphor is not merely transferring the word lion to a different lexical sense; it exaggerates by asserting that the brave man is truly a lion, with the meaning borrowed before the word.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p317/r1.anchor: وأن يدعى في الرجل أنه ليس برجل ، ولكنه أسد بالحقيقة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p317/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p317/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p317/r2.claim: Metaphor is more eloquent than literal comparison because it asserts the quality itself; a mere transfer of a name could not make رأيت أسدا superior to رأيت شبيها بالأسد.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p317/r2.anchor: أن من شأن الاستعارة أن تكون أبدا أبلغ من الحقيقة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p317/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p317/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p317/r3.claim: Analogical naming assigns an object the name of a distinctive quality it fully possesses: a supremely brave man is a lion, exceptional goodness or beauty a king, and utmost fragrance musk. A speaker may deny the original category, as in 12:31, or preserve it with an image such as lion in human form.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p317/r3.anchor: كما قال الله تعالى : ( ﴿ ما هذا بشرا إن هذا إلا ملك ﴾ كريم )

KHATTABI:v1p26/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p26/r1.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p26/r1.claim: Humans cannot match the Qur'an because they lack complete knowledge of Arabic words, their meanings, and the possible patterns of composition needed to choose the best arrangement.
KHATTABI:v1p26/r1.anchor: أن علمهم لا يحيط بجميع أسماء اللغة العربية [وبألفاظها] التى هى ظروف المعانى والحوامل لها

KHATTABI:v1p26/r2.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p26/r2.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p26/r2.claim: Speech is made up of three elements: a word that carries meaning, a meaning borne by it, and a bond that organizes the two.
KHATTABI:v1p26/r2.anchor: وإنما يقوم الكلام بهذه الأشياء الثلاثة: لفظ حامل , ومعنى به قائم , ورباط لهما ناظم

KHATTABI:v1p26/r3.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p26/r3.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p26/r3.claim: The Qur'an reaches the highest degree in all three elements: its words are most eloquent and graceful, its composition most harmonious, and its meanings intellectually preeminent.
KHATTABI:v1p26/r3.anchor: وجدت هذه الأمور منه في غاية الشرف والفضيلة حتى لا ترى شيئا من الألفاظ أفصح ولا أجزل ولا أعذب من ألفاظه

KHATTABI:v1p26/r4.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p26/r4.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p26/r4.claim: These three excellences may occur separately in kinds of speech, but only God's speech combines them, because He knows and counts all things.
KHATTABI:v1p26/r4.anchor: فأما أن توجد مجموعة في نوع واحد منه فلم توجد إلا في كلام العليم القدير

KHATTABI:v1p26/r5.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p26/r5.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p26/r5.claim: The Qur'an is inimitable through the finest diction, best composition, and soundest meanings, spanning monotheism, divine transcendence, worship, law, moral instruction, and ethical guidance.
KHATTABI:v1p26/r5.anchor: أن القرآن إنما صار معجزا لأنه جاء بأفصح الألفاظ في أحسن نظوم التأليف مضمنا أصح المعاني

KHATTABI:v1p26/r6.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p26/r6.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p26/r6.claim: The Qur'an places each subject where nothing else would be more fitting or more appropriate to reason.
KHATTABI:v1p26/r6.anchor: واضعا كل شيء منها موضعه الذي لا يرى شيء أولى منه , ولا يرى في صورة العقل أمر أليق منه

KHATTABI:v1p26/r7.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p26/r7.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p26/r7.claim: Its contents include accounts of past peoples and God's punishments of them, as well as reports about future events across the ages.
KHATTABI:v1p26/r7.anchor: مودعا أخبار القرون الماضية وما نزل من مثلات الله بمن عصى وعاند منهم , منبئا عن الكوائن المستقبلة في الأعصار الباقية من الزمان

KHATTABI:v1p26/r8.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p26/r8.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p26/r8.claim: The Qur'an joins proof to what is proved and evidence to its conclusion, strengthening adherence to its summons and establishing the obligation of its commands and prohibitions.
KHATTABI:v1p26/r8.anchor: جامعا في ذلك بين الحجة والمحتج له , والدليل والمدلول عليه , ليكون ذلك أوكد للزوم مادعا إليه

RUMMANI:v1p73/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p73/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p73/r1.claim: He lists seven aspects of Qur'anic inimitability: lack of countering despite motive and need, universal challenge, ṣarfah, eloquence, true future reports, breaking custom, and comparison with every miracle.
RUMMANI:v1p73/r1.anchor: وجوه إعجاز القرآن تظهر من سبع جهات: ترك المعارضة مع توفر الدواعي وشدة الحاجة , والتحدي للكافة

RUMMANI:v1p73/r2.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p73/r2.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p73/r2.claim: Eloquence has a highest, lowest, and intermediate tier; the Qur'an occupies the highest, miraculous tier, while lower tiers remain possible for human eloquence.
RUMMANI:v1p73/r2.anchor: فما كان في أعلاها طبقة فهو معجز , وهو بلاغة القرآن. وما كان منها دون ذلك فهو ممكن كبلاغة البلغاء من الناس

RUMMANI:v1p73/r3.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p73/r3.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p73/r3.claim: Eloquence is not simply making meaning understood or matching words to meaning, since either can be done in awkward, forced, repellent language; it conveys meaning to the heart in the best verbal form.
RUMMANI:v1p73/r3.anchor: وليست البلاغة إفهام المعنى , لأنه قد يفهم المعنى متكلمان أحدهما بليغ والآخر عيي؛ ولا البلاغة أيضا بتحقيق اللفظ على المعنى

RUMMANI:v1p73/r4.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p73/r4.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p73/r4.claim: The Qur'an's highest eloquence is a miracle for Arabs and non-Arabs alike, whereas a poem that leaves a poet speechless is miraculous only for that particular audience.
RUMMANI:v1p73/r4.anchor: وأعلى طبقات البلاغة للقرآن خاصة , وأعلى طبقات البلاغة معجز للعرب والعجم كإعجاز الشعر المغحم

RUMMANI:v1p73/r5.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p73/r5.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p73/r5.claim: He divides eloquence into ten branches: concision, simile, metaphor, harmony and cadences, paronomasia, taṣrīf, inclusion, hyperbole, and good exposition.
RUMMANI:v1p73/r5.anchor: والبلاغة على عشرة أقسام: الإيجاز , والتشبيه , والاستعارة , والتلاؤم والفواصل , والتجانس , والتصريف , والتضمين , والمبالغة , وحسن البيان

RUMMANI:v1p97/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p97/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p97/r1.claim: Fawāṣil are matching sounds at phrase endings that aid understanding; they are eloquent because meaning guides them, while sajʿ is defective because it makes meaning follow the sound.
RUMMANI:v1p97/r1.anchor: الفواصل حروف متشاكلة في المقاطع توجب حسن إفهام المعاني. والفواصل بلاغة , والأسجاع عيب , وذلك أن الفواصل تابعة للمعاني , وأما الأسجاع فالمعاني تابعة لها

RUMMANI:v1p97/r2.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p97/r2.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p97/r2.claim: When sound patterning does not serve the urgent aim of explaining meaning, it becomes forced and awkward; he likens it to adorning a fallen person or a dog with costly jewelry.
RUMMANI:v1p97/r2.anchor: ومثله مثل من رصع تاجا ثم ألبسه زنجيا ساقطا , أو نظم قلادة در ثم ألبسها كلبا

RUMMANI:v1p97/r3.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p97/r3.speaker: بعض الكهان
RUMMANI:v1p97/r3.claim: He reports a soothsayer's nonsensical rhyme about earth, sky, a crow, and glory fleeing to the camels as an example of bad sajʿ.
RUMMANI:v1p97/r3.anchor: ما يحكى عن بعض الكهان: " والأرض والسماء , والغراب الواقعة بنقعاء

RUMMANI:v1p97/r4.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p97/r4.speaker: مسيلمة الكذاب
RUMMANI:v1p97/r4.claim: He reports Musaylima's rhymed address to a frog as among the emptiest and most foolish speech, illustrating how meaning was subordinated to sound.
RUMMANI:v1p97/r4.anchor: ما يحكى عن مسيلمة الكذاب: " يا ضفدع نقي كم تنقين , لا الماء تكدرين ولا النهر تفارقين

RUMMANI:v1p97/r5.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p97/r5.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p97/r5.claim: All Qur'anic fawāṣil are eloquent and wise, helping communicate needed meanings in the best verbal form.
RUMMANI:v1p97/r5.anchor: وفواصل القرآن كلها بلاغة وحكمة , لأنها طريق إلى إفهام المعاني التي يحتاج إليها في أحسن صورة يدل بها عليها

RUMMANI:v1p97/r6.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p97/r6.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p97/r6.claim: He traces sajʿ to the pigeon's cooing, which has only similar sounds; sound pattern without needed or useful meaning is therefore no better than sound alone.
RUMMANI:v1p97/r6.anchor: وإنما أخذ السجع في الكلام من سجع الحمامة. وذلك أنه ليس فيه إلا الأصوات المتشاكلة

RUMMANI:v1p97/r7.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p97/r7.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p97/r7.claim: Fawāṣil fall into two forms: endings with identical letters and endings with nearby letters.
RUMMANI:v1p97/r7.anchor: والفواصل على وجهين: أحدهما على الحروف المتجانسة والآخر على الحروف المتقاربة

RUMMANI:v1p97/r10.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p97/r10.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p97/r10.claim: Nearby ending letters work because the surrounding discourse clarifies the intended sense and makes the pauses distinguishable, preserving eloquence.
RUMMANI:v1p97/r10.anchor: وإنما حسن في الفواصل الحروف المتقاربة لأنه يكتنف الكلام من البيان ما يدل على المراد في تمييز الفواصل والمقاطع

RUMMANI:v1p97/r11.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p97/r11.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p97/r11.claim: Poetic rhymes cannot rely on this allowance for nearby letters, since rhyme does not belong to the highest tier of eloquence.
RUMMANI:v1p97/r11.anchor: وأما القوافي فلا تحتمل ذلك لأنها ليست في الطبقة العليا من البلاغة

DAMGHANI:v1p49/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r3.claim: For the verse about humanity’s excellent form, al-insān is identified either as Hishām ibn al-Mughīra or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r3.anchor: الإنسان يعني هشام بن المغيرة أو وليد بن المغيرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r2.claim: Some identify the human created in the best form as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra; another view says Hishām ibn al-Mughīra.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r1.speaker: قوم
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r1.claim: Some attribute inimitability to the Qur’an’s values, parables, and rulings, which could not have come from an unlettered person among an unlettered people in that time and place.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r1.anchor: وقال قوم إن إعجاز القرآن بقيمه ومثله وأحكام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r2.claim: The challenge confronted the polytheists in the Meccan period and was settled by the first Medinan sura, before legislation was completed at the end of revelation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r2.anchor: قضية التحدي واجهت المشركين في العهد المكي وحسمت بآية البقرة أولى السور المدنيات

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r3.speaker: الخطابي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r3.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī grounds inimitability in eloquent wording, excellent arrangement, and meanings spanning creed, worship, law, ethics, and guidance, each placed fittingly beyond human capacity.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r3.anchor: الخطابي يقول شرحاً لهذا الوجه من الإعجاز: "وأعلم أن القرآن إنما صار معجزاً لأنه جاء بأفصح الألفاظ

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r4.speaker: الباقلاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r4.claim: Al-Bāqillānī discusses miraculous religious meanings, laws, and arguments, then connects them to the inimitable wording and mutual elegance of their arrangement.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p90/r4.anchor: و"الباقلانى" كتب بعض فقرة في "إعجاز المعاني التي تضمنها، في أصل وضع الشريعة والأحكام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r1.speaker: الرماني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r1.claim: Al-Rummānī divides eloquence into three levels: only the highest, which is Qur’anic eloquence, is miraculous; the middle and lower levels remain possible for human speakers.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r1.anchor: فما كان أعلاها طبقة فهو معجز، وهو بلاغة القرآن. وما كان دون ذلك فهو ممكن كبلاغة البلغاء من الناس

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r2.speaker: الخطابي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r2.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī differs by saying Qur’anic eloquence encompasses all three levels.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r2.anchor: خلافاً لما ذهب إليه أبو سليمان الخطابي من أن بلاغة القرآن تحوز هذه البلاغات في طبقاتها الثلاث

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r3.speaker: الرماني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r3.claim: Al-Rummānī defines eloquence as conveying meaning to the heart in the most beautiful verbal form, not merely making it understood or matching words to meaning.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r3.anchor: وإنما البلاغة إيصال المعنى إلى القلب في أحسن صورة من اللفظ

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r4.speaker: الرماني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r4.claim: Al-Rummānī analyzes Qur’anic eloquence through ten topics: concision, simile, metaphor, harmony, endings, paronomasia, variation, inclusion, amplification, and fine exposition.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r4.anchor: أن جعل البلاغة عشرة أقسام: الإيجاز، والتشبيه، والاستعارة، والتلاؤم، والفواصل، والتجانس، والتصريف، والتضمين، والمبالغة، وحسن البيان

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r5.speaker: الرماني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r5.claim: Ījāz minimizes wording without loss of meaning and divides into omission, where context supplies a dropped word, and concision, where short wording carries abundant meaning without omission.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p104/r5.anchor: تقليل الكلام من غير إخلال بالمعنى. وهو على وجهين: إيجاز حذف، وإيجاز قصر.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r1.speaker: الباقلاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r1.claim: Al-Bāqillānī concedes some incidental Quranic rhyme, which he calls improvised sajʿ, but says this is insufficient to classify the Quran as sajʿ, just as an occasional poetic line does not make prose poetry.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r1.anchor: ويوشك "الباقلاني" في احتجاجه لنفي السجع في القرآن، أن يسلم بقدر منه فيه مما سماه السجع المعتجل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r2.claim: Bint al-Shati finds unconvincing al-Bāqillānī’s distinction between Quranic endings and sajʿ based on differences in the length of their clauses.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r2.anchor: ولا يبدو لنا قويا واضحا، وجه تفريقه بين الفواصل والسجع، من حيث تفاوت المقاطع طولا وقصرا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r3.claim: Allowing sajʿ in the Quran does not require accepting the Muʿtazilite doctrine of ṣarfa; the Muʿtazilites themselves categorically denied Quranic sajʿ.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r3.anchor: وليس حتما على من جوز السجع في القرآن، أن يسلم كما قال الباقلاني بمذهب أصحاب الاعتزال في الإعجاز بالصرفة، فالمعتزلة أنفسهم نفوا السجع عن القرآن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r4.speaker: علي بن عيسى الرماني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r4.claim: Al-Rummani’s stronger account treats Quranic fawāṣil as eloquent, meaning-led endings that convey ideas; sajʿ is defective because it subordinates meaning to sound.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p257/r4.anchor: واحتج منهم "علي بن عيسى الرماني" لهذا النفي بأقوى مما احتج به الأشاعرة، وعدَّ الفواصل القرآنية من وجوه الإعجاز البلاغي للقرآن

GHARNATI:v1p179/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p179/r1.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p179/r1.claim: The invocation praises God for creating the human being in the best form after a drop of semen, then honoring the human being and preparing him to receive revelation.
GHARNATI:v1p179/r1.anchor: وخلقه في أحسن تقويم بعد كون

ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r1.speaker: النخعي ومجاهد وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r1.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi, Mujahid, and Qatada understand the best formation as beauty of form and senses.
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r1.anchor: قال النخعي ومجاهد وقتادة : حسن صورته وحواسه

ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r2.claim: Another view takes the best formation to mean an erect stature.

ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r3.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says human intellect and perception were adorned by discernment.
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r3.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر : عقله وإدراكه زيناه بالتمييز

ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r4.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r4.claim: ʿIkrima explains it as youth and strength.

ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the general sense, encompassing everything that is best in the human constitution.
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r5.anchor: والأولى العموم في كل ما هو أحسن

ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r6.claim: Here الإنسان is a generic noun referring to the human species.

ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r7.claim: أحسن is an adjective of an omitted noun: the human is in a better or best formation.
ABUHAYYAN:95:4/r7.anchor: والإنسان هنا اسم جنس ، وأحسن صفة لمحذوف ، أي في تقويم أحسن

ALUSI:95:4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:4/r1.claim: Al-insān means the human species, including believer and unbeliever, rather than only the disbeliever; the valid exception in the following verse and the default connected sense support this.
ALUSI:95:4/r1.anchor: وأريد بالإنسان الجنس فهو شامل للمؤمن والكافر لا مخصوص بالثاني واستدل عليه بصحة الاستثناء وأن الأصل فيه الاتصال

ALUSI:95:4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:4/r2.claim: The phrase is a circumstantial expression describing the human as being in the best constitution; taqwīm means God's act of correction and adjustment.
ALUSI:95:4/r2.anchor: في موضع الحال من الإنسان أي كائناً في تقويم أحسن تقويم والتقويم التثقيف والتعديل وهو فعل الله عز وجل

ALUSI:95:4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:4/r3.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI:95:4/r3.claim: Al-Khafājī construes the phrase by supplying a noun such as uprightness or the one made upright, yielding the construct phrase the uprightness of the best form.
ALUSI:95:4/r3.anchor: وقال الخفاجي هو مؤول بمعنى القوام أو المقوم وفيه مضاف مقدر أي قوام أحسن تقويم

ALUSI:95:4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:4/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:95:4/r4.claim: Another parsing treats fī as extra and the following words as an absolute object, with its adjective standing in for the verbal noun: God shaped him with the best shaping.
ALUSI:95:4/r4.anchor: أو في زائدة وما بعدها في موضع المفعول المطلق وقد ناب فيه عن المصدر صفته والتقدير قومناه تقويماً أحسن تقويم

ALUSI:95:4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:4/r5.claim: The best form includes the finest physical and inward qualities: upright stature, beauty, perception, sound intellect, and more.
ALUSI:95:4/r5.anchor: والمراد بذلك جعله على أحسن ما يكون صورة ومعنى فيشمل ماله من انتصاب القامة وحسن الصورة والإحساس وجودة العقل

ALUSI:95:4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:4/r6.claim: The human is a comprehensive microcosm joining the seen and unseen, giving and receiving, and containing the wonders of creation and all that was and will be; a poem attributed to ʿAlī says the greater world is folded within him.
ALUSI:95:4/r6.anchor: مجمع مجرى الغيب والشهادة ومطلع نيري فلكي الإفادة والاستفادة والنسخة الجامعة لما في رسائل إخوان الصفا

ALUSI:95:4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:4/r7.speaker: علي
ALUSI:95:4/r7.claim: A line attributed to ʿAlī says a person's cure and disease are within, and that although one imagines oneself a small body, the greater world is folded within.
ALUSI:95:4/r7.anchor: ونسب لعلي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI:95:4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:4/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:4/r8.claim: The human form recalls and points to divine attributes: God made the human knowing, willing, and powerful, and the saying to take on God's qualities answers the concern that such attributes are forbidden to servants.
ALUSI:95:4/r8.anchor: إن الله تعالى رسم فيه من الصفات ما تذكره صفاته عز وجل وتدله عليها فجعله عالماً مريداً قادراً

ALUSI:95:4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:4/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:4/r9.claim: As further evidence of human honor, God says He created Adam with His two hands and ordered the honored angels to prostrate to him.
ALUSI:95:4/r9.anchor: ويكفي في هذا الباب وهو القول الفصل إن الله تعالى خلقه بيديه وأمر سبحانه ملائكته عليهم السلام بالسجود له

ALUSI:95:4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:4/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:95:4/r10.claim: The source cites the report that God created Adam in His image, with another version saying in the image of the Merciful, and argues that the latter rules out taking the pronoun to refer to Adam.
ALUSI:95:4/r10.anchor: وجاء إن الله تعالى خلق آدم على صورته وفي رواية على صورة الرحمن وهي تأبى احتمال عود الضمير على آدم

ALUSI:95:4/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:4/r11.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
ALUSI:95:4/r11.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh al-Rāzī says that whoever knows himself knows his Lord; people call it a hadith, but al-Nawawī says it is not established as one.
ALUSI:95:4/r11.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ الرازي من عرف نفسه فقد عرف ربه والناس يزعمونه حديثاً وليس كما قال النووي بثابت

ALUSI:95:4/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:95:4/r12.speaker: يحيى بن أكثم
ALUSI:95:4/r12.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Aktham and some Hanafis reportedly ruled that a conditional divorce took effect when a husband said his wife would be divorced if she were not fairer than the moon, citing this verse; al-Ālūsī says the distinction is obvious.
ALUSI:95:4/r12.anchor: وعن يحيى بن أكثم وبعض الحنفية أنهما أفتيا من قال لزوجته إن لم تكوني أحسن من القمر فأنت طالق بعد وقوع الطلاق

BAGHAWI:95:4/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:4/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:95:4/r1.claim: The preceding material consists of oaths, and this verse states what is sworn to: God created humanity in the best form.
BAGHAWI:95:4/r1.anchor: هذه كلها أقسام ، والمقسم عليه قوله :{ لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم }

BAGHAWI:95:4/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:95:4/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:95:4/r2.claim: Best form means upright stature and the finest appearance: unlike other animals, humans stand tall, use their hands to take food, and have reason and discernment.
BAGHAWI:95:4/r2.anchor: أعدل قامة وأحسن صورة ، وذلك أنه خلق كل حيوان منكباً على وجهه إلا الإنسان خلقه مديد القامة ، يتناول مأكوله بيده

BAGHAWI:103:3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:103:3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:103:3/r7.claim: Baghawi connects Ibrahim’s account of believers retaining their good works in old age with the passage about creation in the best form and the exception of believers from being brought low.
BAGHAWI:103:3/r7.anchor: وهي مثل قوله : { لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم * ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين * إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات }

BAYDAWI:95:4/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:95:4/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:95:4/r1.claim: Al-insān here means humankind as a genus.

BAYDAWI:95:4/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:95:4/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:95:4/r2.claim: The best proportion includes upright stature, beautiful form, and a gathering of the distinctive properties of beings and other possible things.
BAYDAWI:95:4/r2.anchor: بانتصاب القامة ، وحسن الصورة ، واستجماع خواص الكائنات

BIQAI:95:4/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r1.claim: The human kind gathers wondrous created features that demonstrate the Creator's knowledge and power and includes many believers; Abraham, their father, is twice associated with the holy land, Jerusalem and Mecca, preparing for the response to the oath.
BIQAI:95:4/r1.anchor: جامعاً لبدائع المصنوعات التي هي لما ذكر من حكمها دالة على كمال علم خالقها وتمام قدرته

BIQAI:95:4/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r2.claim: The verb means that God determined and brought the human species into existence by His overwhelming greatness and might.
BIQAI:95:4/r2.anchor: أي قدرنا وأوجدنا بما لنا من العظمة الباهرة والعزة الغالبة القاهرة

BIQAI:95:4/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r3.claim: The human species combines desire and intellect and self-familiarity that can distract a person from important concerns.
BIQAI:95:4/r3.anchor: هذا النوع الذي جمع فيه الشهوة والعقل وفيه الأنس بنفسه ما ينسيه أكثر مهمه

BIQAI:95:4/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r4.claim: The angels' question about creating one who will corrupt and shed blood reflects their awareness that anger and desire combined with intellect produce conflict, corruption from desire, and bloodshed from anger.
BIQAI:95:4/r4.anchor: لأنهم علموا أنه إذا جمع الغضب والشهوة إلى العقل جاءت المنازعة

BIQAI:95:4/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r5.claim: Best stature encompasses spirit and intellect, or more broadly the whole human: upright posture, beauty, sensory capacities suited to life's purpose, and a gathering of qualities found across created beings; thus man is called the microcosm.
BIQAI:95:4/r5.anchor: بما جعلنا له من حسن الخلق والخلق بما خص به من انتصاب القامة

BIQAI:95:4/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r6.claim: God endowed humans with an original, sound nature, unchanged in its first disposition and prepared to receive truth.
BIQAI:95:4/r6.anchor: الفطرة الأولى التي لا تبديل لها من الطبع الأول السليم الذي هيأناه به

BIQAI:95:4/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r7.speaker: الأصفهاني
BIQAI:95:4/r7.claim: Al-Aṣfahānī likewise explains the verse about people being one community through the original human disposition.

BIQAI:95:4/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r8.speaker: ابن برجان
BIQAI:95:4/r8.claim: Ibn Barrajān says the human is naturally formed upon Islam, the upright religion.
BIQAI:95:4/r8.anchor: وقال ابن برجان هنا : مفطور على فطرة الإسلام

BIQAI:95:4/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r9.claim: With reason, God enables people to rise from Hell's depths to the gardens through faith and excellent deeds; prophets, especially Muhammad, and his learned, wise, luminous followers show this human potential.
BIQAI:95:4/r9.anchor: منحناه عقلاً يهديه إلى العروج عن درك النيران إلى درج الجنان بالإيمان والأعمال الصالحة

BIQAI:95:4/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r10.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI:95:4/r10.claim: Al-Baghawī describes the human as tall, eating with his hand, and adorned with reason and discernment.
BIQAI:95:4/r10.anchor: قال البغوي : خلقه سبحانه وتعالى مديد القامة يتناول مأكوله بيده

BIQAI:95:4/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r11.claim: Reason is humanity's true purpose and is called its lubb, or core; the author connects the core purpose of things with divine law, as discussed at the end of al-Nisāʾ.
BIQAI:95:4/r11.anchor: والعقل هو المقصود في الحقيقة من الإنسان لأن من أسمائه اللب

BIQAI:95:4/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r12.claim: Human intellects are broadly comparable, but innate dispositions vary: temperament can undermine reason, while people may be astute in one subject and dull in another; these differences organize human livelihoods and crafts.
BIQAI:95:4/r12.anchor: والظاهر أن عقول الناس بحسب الخلق متقاربة

BIQAI:95:4/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r13.speaker: الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري
BIQAI:95:4/r13.claim: Al-Qushayrī argues that God is transcendent above composition and form: if He had a shared attribute such as form, He would be the best instance of it, since the Creator surpasses creation in shared attributes.
BIQAI:95:4/r13.anchor: قاله الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري في تفسيره

BIQAI:95:4/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r14.claim: The author rejects the claim attributed to some elders that nothing more excellent than the existing world is possible; levels can vary without limit, as human forms and colors already show.
BIQAI:95:4/r14.anchor: وصيغة  "  أفعل  "  لا تدل على ما قاله الزنادقة

BIQAI:95:4/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r15.claim: Alternatively, best may be relative to something God wills us to recognize; Sunni doctrine, stated by al-Ashʿarī and al-Ghazālī, holds that God's possible acts are limitless.
BIQAI:95:4/r15.anchor: ويمكن أن تكون صيغة أفعل مفيدة بالنسبة إلى شيء أراده الله بحيث إن نتفطن له نحن

BIQAI:95:4/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r16.claim: Al-Ghazālī identifies the philosophers' denial of God's will and claim that He acts by necessity as the source of their error; he affirms God's power over every possible thing.
BIQAI:95:4/r16.anchor: وبين أن هذا من قواعدهم لنفيهم صفة الإرادة

BIQAI:95:4/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:4/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:4/r17.claim: A possible thing is whatever God can bring about; impossibility means affirming a thing while denying it, or affirming a specific or two while denying its general category or one. Thus a more excellent world is possible, and God can create other worlds of different sizes.
BIQAI:95:4/r17.anchor: وعرف أن الممكن هو المقدور عليه

DURR:95:4/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:95:4/r4.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas identifies fig and olive with the Sacred Mosque and al-Aqsa, Sinai as the mountain Moses ascended, and the secure city as Mecca; he says humans were created upright rather than face-down and later reach old age.
DURR:95:4/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { والتين والزيتون } قال : هما المسجدان مسجد الحرام ومسجد الأقصى

DURR:95:4/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR:95:4/r5.claim: Qatada maps the oath to Damascus, Jerusalem, a blessed tree-covered Syrian mountain, and Mecca; he says its answer is 95:4, the lowest state is Hell, and the judgment question calls for certainty because God’s proof came.
DURR:95:4/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { والتين } قال : التين الجبل الذي عليه دمشق

DURR:95:4/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r15.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:95:4/r15.claim: Mujahid explains the best stature as the best form.
DURR:95:4/r15.anchor: { لقد خلقنا الإِنسان في أحسن تقويم } قال : في أحسن صورة

DURR:95:4/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r23.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:95:4/r23.claim: Ibn Abbas calls human creation the most equitable form.
DURR:95:4/r23.anchor: عن ابن عباس { لقد خلقنا الإِنسان في أحسن تقويم } قال : في أعدل خلق

DURR:95:4/r25.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r25.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:95:4/r25.claim: Ibn Abbas contrasts humans, created upright, with everything else, created face-down.
DURR:95:4/r25.anchor: عن ابن عباس { لقد خلقنا الإِنسان في أحسن تقويم } قال : خلق كل شيء منكبّاً على وجهه إلا الإنسان

DURR:95:4/r28.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r28.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:95:4/r28.claim: Ikrima explains the best stature as youth and strength.
DURR:95:4/r28.anchor: { لقد خلقنا الإِنسان في أحسن تقويم } قال : شباب وشدة

DURR:95:4/r31.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r31.speaker: الحسن
DURR:95:4/r31.claim: Al-Hasan explains the best stature as the best form.
DURR:95:4/r31.anchor: { لقد خلقنا الإِنسان في أحسن تقويم } قال : في أحسن صورة

DURR:95:4/r33.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r33.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR:95:4/r33.claim: Abu al-Aliya explains the best stature as the best image.
DURR:95:4/r33.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله : { لقد خلقنا الإِنسان في أحسن تقويم } يقول : في أحسن صورة

DURR:95:4/r35.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:95:4/r35.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR:95:4/r35.claim: Ibrahim explains the best stature as the best image.
DURR:95:4/r35.anchor: عن إبراهيم { قد خلقنا الإِنسان في أحسن تقويم } قال : في أحسن صورة

IBNASHUR:95:4/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r1.claim: The clause, together with what is coordinated with it, answers the preceding oath; the oath stresses a hidden formation and hidden return that require reflection.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r1.anchor: وجملة : { لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم } مع ما عطف عليه هو جواب القسم

IBNASHUR:95:4/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r2.claim: The oath is apt because many people's beliefs and conduct resemble those of people who deny that they were created upon the fitrah.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r2.anchor: لأن تصرفات معظم الناس في عقائدهم جارية على حالة تشبه حالة من ينكرون أنهم خُلقوا على الفطرة

IBNASHUR:95:4/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r3.claim: Creation means bringing something into being; God created all people by originating the first sources of life and creating the causes by which descendants reproduce.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r3.anchor: والخلق : تكوين وإيجاد لشيء ، وخلق الله جميع الناس هو أنه خلق أصول الإيجاد وأوجد الأصول الأولى

IBNASHUR:95:4/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r4.claim: The definite noun may be generic, referring to humanity collectively and thus meaning that God created all people in the best constitution.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r4.anchor: ويحمل على معنى : خلقنا جميع الناس في أحسن تقويم

IBNASHUR:95:4/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r5.claim: Alternatively, the definite noun can denote the human essence in its original state, without attending to individual traits that alter it; Ibn Ashur compares this to a proverb and poetry.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تعريف { الإنسان } تعريف الحقيقة نحو قولهم : الرجل خير من المرأة ، وقول امرىء القيس : الحرب أول ما تكون فَتية

IBNASHUR:95:4/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r6.claim: Taqwim is making something upright and balanced; the best constitution is the most complete and fitting constitution for the human kind.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r6.anchor: والتقويم : جعل الشيء في قَوام ( بفتح القاف ) ، أي عَدل وتسوية ، وحسن التقويم أكمله وأليقه بنوع الإِنسان

IBNASHUR:95:4/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r7.claim: Human constitution is uniquely apt: outward and inward faculties are balanced so none corrupts the person or prevents another from doing its work; other creatures are lower in this respect.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r7.anchor: تقويم خاص بالإِنسان لا يشاركه فيه غيره من المخلوقات ، ويتضح ذلك في تعديل القوى الظاهرة والباطنة

IBNASHUR:95:4/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r8.claim: Fi is metaphorical containment for firm attachment or possession, functioning like bi of accompaniment or lam of possession; the choice adds force while remaining concise.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r8.anchor: وحرف { في } يفيد الظرفية المجازية المستعارة لمعنى التمكن والمِلك فهي مستعملة في معنى باء الملابسة أو لام الملك

IBNASHUR:95:4/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r9.claim: God fashioned the human being inwardly in a coordinated way suited to the species' capacities for social order and civilization.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r9.anchor: أن الله كوَّن الإِنسان تكويناً ذاتياً مُتناسباً ما خلق له نوعه من الإِعداد لنظامه وحضارته

IBNASHUR:95:4/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r10.claim: Physical appearance is not the intended constitution: it does not reform the soul, other people, or the earth, and making it central would break the fit between the oath and the surah's subject.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r10.anchor: وليس تقويم صورة الإِنسان الظاهرة هو المعتبر عند الله تعالى ولا جديراً بأن يقسم عليه إذ لا أثر له في إصلاح النفس

IBNASHUR:95:4/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:95:4/r11.claim: A Prophetic report says God looks at people's hearts rather than their bodies or images; Ibn Ashur cites it in support of prioritizing inward constitution. Muslim transmits it, with other versions adding wording.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r11.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم « إن الله لا ينظر إلى أجسادكم ولا إلى صوركم ولكن ينظر إلى قلوبكم »

IBNASHUR:95:4/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r12.claim: The intended excellence is sound human perception and rational judgment, since bodily actions issue from the intellect and the body serves it; intellect is humanity's noblest distinguishing gift.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r12.anchor: فالمرضيّ عند الله هو تقويم إدراك الإِنسان ونظره العقلي الصحيح لأن ذلك هو الذي تصدر عنه أعمال الجسد

IBNASHUR:95:4/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r13.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNASHUR:95:4/r13.claim: Many exegetes explain the return to the lowest state as loss of strength in old age; Ibn Ashur says this reading fits the surah's purpose even less and hardly warrants an oath.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r13.anchor: لو حمل الرد أسفل سافلين على مصير الإِنسان في أرذل العمر إلى نقائص قوته كما فسر به كثير من المفسرين

IBNASHUR:95:4/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r14.claim: The exception for believers supports an inward reading: faith follows the intellect's sound constitution, which guides upright conduct and good dealings with people who do not oppose it.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r14.anchor: ويدل لذلك قوله بعده : { إلا الذين آمنوا } [ التين : 6 ] لأن الإِيمان أثر التقويم لعقل الإنسان

IBNASHUR:95:4/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r15.claim: The original constitution can be impaired before birth by parental illness or injury during pregnancy, and after birth by severe disease, deranged temperament, intoxicants, or drugs that weaken reason and resolve.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r15.anchor: إما من عاهة تلحقه لمرض أحد الأبوين ، أو لفساد هيكله من سقطة أو صدمة في حمله ، وما يعرض له بعد الولادة

IBNASHUR:95:4/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r16.claim: Humans are created with complete human fitrah: sound senses deliver truthful perceptions, and a sound mind analyzes and combines them correctly, yielding upright conduct if not diverted or if false influences are resisted.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r16.anchor: وهي الفطرة الإنسانية الكاملة في إدراكه إدراكاً مستقيماً مما يتأدى من المحسوسات الصادقة

IBNASHUR:95:4/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r17.claim: People can be led astray by vanity and desire or by misleaders using fear and inducement; repeated imitation becomes habitual until they forget what is true and right.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r17.anchor: فترمي به في الضلالات ، أو يتغلب عليه دعاة الضلال بعامل التخويف أو الإطماع فيتابعهم طوعاً أو كرهاً

IBNASHUR:95:4/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r18.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:95:4/r18.claim: The Prophet reports that every newborn is born upon fitrah, then parents make the child Jewish, Christian, or Magian; no grading is stated here.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r18.anchor: ويفسر هذا المعنى قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم « ما من مولود إلا يولد على الفطرة ثم يكون أبواه هما اللذان يهوِّدانه

IBNASHUR:95:4/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r19.claim: Parents are named because they first educate the child, remain closest during childhood, and most strongly and persistently introduce beliefs; later influences may also be good or bad.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r19.anchor: واقتصر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الأبوين لأنهما أقوى أسباب الزج في ضلالتهما ، وأشد إلحاحاً على ولدهما

IBNASHUR:95:4/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r20.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة، الكلبي، إبراهيم، أبو العالية
IBNASHUR:95:4/r20.claim: These authorities are reported as interpreting the best constitution as beautiful physical form, a restriction Ibn Ashur says does not suit the surah's purpose unless treated as a rejected blessing.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r20.anchor: فقصروا التقويم على حسن الصورة . وروي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والكلبي

IBNASHUR:95:4/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:95:4/r21.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas interprets the best constitution as upright stature; Ibn Ashur finds such bodily readings ill-suited to the surah's purpose.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r21.anchor: أو على استقامة القامة . وروي عن ابن عباس

IBNASHUR:95:4/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r22.speaker: عكرمة، ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:95:4/r22.claim: Ikrimah and Ibn Abbas are reported to interpret the phrase as youth and vigor, another outward reading that Ibn Ashur regards as ill-suited to the surah's purpose.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r22.anchor: أو على الشباب والجلادة ، وروي عن عكرمة وابن عباس

IBNASHUR:95:4/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r23.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
IBNASHUR:95:4/r23.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir is reported as defining human constitution as the intellect and perception endowed with discernment, close to Ibn Ashur's inward interpretation.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r23.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن طاهر{[457]} أنه قال : « تقويم الإنسان عقله وإدراكه

IBNASHUR:95:4/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r24.speaker: الأصم
IBNASHUR:95:4/r24.claim: Al-Asamm is reported as taking the phrase to mean the fullest intellect, understanding, manners, knowledge, and eloquence, close to Ibn Ashur's inward interpretation.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r24.anchor: وما حكاه الفخر عن الأصم{[458]} أن { أحسن تقويم } أكمل عقل وفهم وأدب وعلم

IBNASHUR:95:4/r25.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r25.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r25.claim: Fitrah inclines people to benefit and reform, justice, helping the distressed and weak, kind treatment, and respect for wise and righteous counsel, provided selfish urges do not interfere.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r25.anchor: وتفيد الآية أن الإِنسان مفطور على الخير وأن في جبلته جلب النفع والصلاح لنفسه وكراهة ما يظنّه باطلاً أو هلاكاً

IBNASHUR:95:4/r26.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r26.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:95:4/r26.claim: When a bad desire overpowers reason, people turn to harmful acts and find advice burdensome; their aversion to counsel varies with the power of passion over intellect.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r26.anchor: وثقْل عليه نصح الناصحين ، ووعظُ الواعظين على مراتب في كراهية ذلك بمقدار تحكم الهوى في عقله

IBNASHUR:95:4/r27.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:95:4/r27.speaker: جمهور الفقهاء والمحدِّثين
IBNASHUR:95:4/r27.claim: The majority of jurists and hadith scholars hold that people are presumptively good, upright, sound in judgment, and well-intentioned.
IBNASHUR:95:4/r27.anchor: ولهذا كان الأصل في الناس الخيرَ والعدالة والرشد وحسن النية عند جمهور من الفقهاء والمحدِّثين

IBNHIBBAN:1838/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1838/r1.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNHIBBAN:1838/r1.claim: Al-Barāʾ reports that the Prophet recited Sūrat al-Tīn in one of the two ʿIshāʾ rakʿahs while traveling.
IBNHIBBAN:1838/r1.anchor: أنه كان في سفر، فقرأ في العشاء، في إحدى الركعتين ب: [التين والزيتون]

IBNATIYYA:95:4/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r1.claim: Human beings are created in an excellent proportion suited to them; this does not preclude other creatures, such as the sun, from being better proportioned in a particular respect.
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r1.anchor: { لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم } ينبغي له ،   ولا يدفع هذا أن يكون غيره من المخلوقات كالشمس وغيرها أحسن تقويماً منه بالمناسبة

IBNATIYYA:95:4/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r2.claim: Some scholars take the statement universally: humankind is the best proportioned of all creatures.
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r2.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء بالعموم أي { الإنسان } أحسن المخلوقات تقويماً

IBNATIYYA:95:4/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r3.claim: Some did not consider a divorce oath broken when a man swore his wife was more beautiful than the sun, arguing from this verse.
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r3.anchor: ولم ير قوم الحنث على من حلف بالطلاق أن زوجته أحسن من الشمس ،   واحتجوا بهذه الآية

IBNATIYYA:95:4/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r4.speaker: النخعي ومجاهد وقتادة
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r4.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī, Mujāhid, and Qatāda say the best proportion means beauty of form and senses.
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r4.anchor: فقال النخعي ومجاهد وقتادة : حسن صورته وحواسه

IBNATIYYA:95:4/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r5.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r5.claim: Another view identifies the best proportion as an upright posture.

IBNATIYYA:95:4/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r6.claim: Abū Bakr ibn Ṭāhir, in al-Thaʿlabī's book, identifies it as intellect and perception that equip people to distinguish.
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r6.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر في كتاب الثعلبي : هو عقله وإدراكه اللذان زيناه بالتمييز

IBNATIYYA:95:4/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r7.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r7.claim: ʿIkrima says it means youth and strength, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this because some animals surpass humans in those traits.
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r7.anchor: وقال عكرمة : هو الشباب والقوة ،   والصواب أن جميع هذا هو حسن التقويم إلا قول عكرمة

IBNATIYYA:95:4/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r8.claim: He holds that form, senses, upright stature, intellect, and perception together constitute excellent proportion; he excludes ʿIkrima's account.
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r8.anchor: والصواب أن جميع هذا هو حسن التقويم إلا قول عكرمة ،   إذا قوله يفضل فيه بعض الحيوان

IBNATIYYA:95:4/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r9.claim: Al-insān here is a generic noun.

IBNATIYYA:95:4/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r10.claim: The construction implies 'in a proportion of the best proportion,' since a superlative adjective must modify an expressed or understood noun.
IBNATIYYA:95:4/r10.anchor: وتقدير الكلام في تقويم { أحسن تقويم } ،   لأن { أحسن } صفة لا بد أن تجري على موصوف

MAWARDI:95:4/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:4/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:95:4/r1.claim: One view takes humankind collectively, using the singular for emphasis because the quality described applies to everyone.
MAWARDI:95:4/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنه أراد عموم الناس ،   وذكر الإنسان على وجه التكثير لأنه وصفه بما يعم لجميع الناس

MAWARDI:95:4/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:4/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:95:4/r2.claim: Alternatively, it may refer to one particular person who is described by a quality shared by people generally.
MAWARDI:95:4/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه أراد إنساناً بعينه عناه بهذه الصفة ،   وإن كان صفة الناس

MAWARDI:95:4/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:95:4/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the particular person as Kulda ibn Asīd.
MAWARDI:95:4/r3.anchor: أحدها : أنه عنى كلدة بن أسيد ،   قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI:95:4/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:4/r4.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI:95:4/r4.claim: Muqātil identifies him as Abū Jahl.

MAWARDI:95:4/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:4/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:95:4/r5.claim: A further identification in the surviving text is the Messenger of God.
MAWARDI:95:4/r5.anchor: الخامس : أنه عنى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI:95:4/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:4/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:95:4/r6.claim: The phrase means the most balanced form of creation.
MAWARDI:95:4/r6.anchor: أحدها : في أعدل خلق ،   قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI:95:4/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:4/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
MAWARDI:95:4/r7.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya interprets it as the finest image.
MAWARDI:95:4/r7.anchor: الثاني : في أحسن صورة ،   قاله أبو العالية

MAWARDI:95:4/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:4/r8.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI:95:4/r8.claim: ʿIkrima takes it to mean youth and strength.
MAWARDI:95:4/r8.anchor: الثالث : في شباب وقوة ،   قاله عكرمة

MAWARDI:95:4/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:4/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:95:4/r9.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās says it means upright stature, unlike other animals, which are bent over.
MAWARDI:95:4/r9.anchor: الرابع : منتصب القامة ،   لأن سائر الحيوان منكب غير الإنسان ،   فإنه منتصب ،   وهو مروي عن ابن عباس

MAWARDI:95:4/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:4/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI:95:4/r10.claim: Māwardī also suggests the most complete intellect, since a person's proper formation rests on reason.
MAWARDI:95:4/r10.anchor: ويحتمل خامساً : أي في أكمل عقل ،   لأن تقويم الإنسان بعقله ،   وعلى هذا وقع القسم

MAWARDI:95:4/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:95:4/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI:95:4/r11.claim: On the interpretation that human perfection lies in intellect, the oath is directed to that point.
MAWARDI:95:4/r11.anchor: لأن تقويم الإنسان بعقله ،   وعلى هذا وقع القسم

NASAFI:95:4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:95:4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:95:4/r1.claim: This is the answer to the oath, and “human” denotes the species as a whole.
NASAFI:95:4/r1.anchor: وجواب القسم { لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنسان } وهو جنس

NASAFI:95:4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:95:4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:95:4/r2.claim: God created the human in the finest proportion: the best form, appearance, and arrangement of limbs.
NASAFI:95:4/r2.anchor: { فِى أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ } في أحسن تعديل لشكله وصورته وتسوية أعضائه

QURTUBI:95:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:95:4/r1.claim: The human in this oath's answer means the unbeliever; on this reading the verse concerns deniers of resurrection.
QURTUBI:95:4/r1.anchor: هذا جواب القسم ، وأراد بالإنسان : الكافر

QURTUBI:95:4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:4/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:95:4/r2.claim: One reported identification of the unbelieving human is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.

QURTUBI:95:4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:4/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:95:4/r3.claim: Another reported identification of the unbelieving human is Kalda ibn Asid.

QURTUBI:95:4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:4/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:95:4/r4.claim: A further view takes the human as Adam and his descendants.

QURTUBI:95:4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:95:4/r5.claim: Most commentators understand the best stature as human balance and uprightness in full youth: other creatures face down, while humans stand upright with articulate tongues and grasping hands and fingers.
QURTUBI:95:4/r5.anchor: وهو اعتداله واستواء شبابه ، كذا قال عامة المفسرين .

QURTUBI:95:4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:4/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
QURTUBI:95:4/r6.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir describes humans as adorned with reason, responsive to commands, discerning, tall, and able to take food by hand.
QURTUBI:95:4/r6.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر : مزينا بالعقل ، مؤديا للأمر

QURTUBI:95:4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:4/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI:95:4/r7.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says no creation is more beautiful: humans possess life, knowledge, power, will, speech, hearing, sight, governance, and wisdom; the report that Adam was created upon God's image refers to such qualities, since God has no corporeal image.
QURTUBI:95:4/r7.anchor: ابن العربي : ليس لله تعالى خلق أحسن من الإنسان ، فإن الله خلقه حيا عالما

QURTUBI:95:4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:4/r8.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI:95:4/r8.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the version upon the Merciful's image cannot imply a particularized divine form; it must refer to meanings or qualities.
QURTUBI:95:4/r8.anchor: وفي رواية [ على صورة الرحمن ] ومن أين تكون للرحمن صورة متشخصة

QURTUBI:95:4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:95:4/r9.claim: In an anecdote, a Hanafi jurist held that a husband's oath to divorce unless his wife was more beautiful than the moon did not take effect, since humans are the most beautiful things; al-Mansur accepted his ruling.
QURTUBI:95:4/r9.anchor: فقال له الرجل : بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم : " والتين والزيتون . وطور سينين

QURTUBI:95:4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:4/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:95:4/r10.claim: The verse shows humans are God's most beautiful creation inside and out, with a finely composed head, chest, belly, sexual organs, hands, and legs.
QURTUBI:95:4/r10.anchor: فهذا يدلك على أن الإنسان أحسن خلق الله باطنا وظاهرا ، جمال هيئة

QURTUBI:95:4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:95:4/r11.speaker: الفلاسفة
QURTUBI:95:4/r11.claim: Philosophers call the human the microcosm because all that is in creation is gathered in the human.
QURTUBI:95:4/r11.anchor: ولذلك قالت الفلاسفة : إنه العالم الأصغر ؛ إذ كل ما في المخلوقات جمع فيه

RAZI:95:4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:95:4/r1.claim: Al-insān means humankind as a kind; taqwīm is shaping a thing as it should be, through proper composition and proportion.
RAZI:95:4/r1.anchor: المراد من الإنسان هذه الماهية والتقويم تصبير الشيء على ما ينبغي أن يكون في التألف والتعديل

RAZI:95:4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:95:4/r2.claim: One explanation is that other living creatures are face-down, while humans stand upright and take food with their hands; this concerns outward form.
RAZI:95:4/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى خلق كل ذي روح مكبا على وجهه إلا الإنسان فإنه تعالى خلقه مديد القامة يتناول مأكوله بيده

RAZI:95:4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:4/r3.speaker: الأصم
RAZI:95:4/r3.claim: Al-Aṣamm interprets the best proportion as complete intellect, understanding, manners, knowledge and eloquence, addressing inner character rather than outward form.
RAZI:95:4/r3.anchor: الأصم : في أكمل عقل وفهم وأدب وعلم وبيان

RAZI:95:4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:4/r4.speaker: يحيى بن أكثم
RAZI:95:4/r4.claim: Yaḥyā b. Aktham interprets taqwīm as beauty of form; in a moonlit conditional divorce case, he alone ruled that the husband had not broken his oath, citing this verse.
RAZI:95:4/r4.anchor: يحيى بن أكثم القاضي أنه فسر التقويم بحسن الصورة

RAZI:95:4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:4/r5.speaker: يحيى بن أكثم
RAZI:95:4/r5.claim: All jurists but Yaḥyā b. Aktham ruled that the husband had broken his oath; Yaḥyā said he had not.
RAZI:95:4/r5.anchor: إلا يحيى بن أكثم فإنه قال : لا يحنث

RAZI:95:4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:95:4/r6.speaker: بعض الصالحين
RAZI:95:4/r6.claim: A pious person prays that God who gave humans their best forms in this world will give them their best deeds in the next: pardon and overlooking faults.
RAZI:95:4/r6.anchor: بعض الصالحين يقول : إلهنا أعطيتنا في الأولى

BIQAI:95:5/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:5/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:5/r1.claim: Though endowed with excellent form, humans face desires and ignoble traits that ruin most of them; this displays God's power and applies to the species as a whole.
BIQAI:95:5/r1.anchor: وكان أكثر الخلق بها هالكاً لتتبين قدرة الله سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI:95:6/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:95:6/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:95:6/r5.claim: God preserves this small group on the original nature of the best form, keeping desire from tainting it, so they follow the messengers and embody justice, beneficence, and noble conduct.
BIQAI:95:6/r5.anchor: بما كملناهم به وشرفناهم على جميع الحيوانات
